review_status: draft v1 - deepwater continental slope grouper

profile.behavior: Deepwater bottom dweller that inhabits rocky drop-offs, mud-bottom mounds, and canyons along the continental slope.

factors.value_notes: The available numeric temperature observations are from spawning-condition females at deep bottom depths (175–223 m) and report 9–15 °C, not surface temperature. No traceable source was found validating the configured 12–24 °C SST range or 14–20 °C ideal. The factor is an active input, but surface temperature is not established as a valid proxy for this deep-water species.

factors.reason_template: Seafloor drops steeply ({value} m/km), forming continental slope drop-offs.
factors.value_notes: SAFMC describes snowy grouper habitat on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, including ridges, terraces, and precipitous cliffs. This supports a broad slope/relief association, but does not validate the pipeline's continuous bottom_slope metric or the assumption that higher slope is always more suitable.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in deep continental slope habitat.
factors.value_notes: SAFMC reports adult depths of 116–259 m on the southeastern U.S. shelf/slope; a spawning survey recorded females at 175–223 m (N=48); FWC describes reef/rocky habitat to 1,700 ft. This supports the configured 100–400 m / 150–280 m band as broad deep-water context, but not a locally calibrated depth optimum. Depth is an active gate.
